# Material Design 3 Motion — Canonical Durations & Easing

## Important note on sourcing

The two m3.material.io pages you linked could not be fetched as documents — `m3.material.io` is a JavaScript-rendered single-page app, so `webfetch` receives only a `<noscript>` stub. The "easing-and-applying-motion" sub-page returns 404 (that URL does not exist at the published path). The legacy m2 `material.io/design/motion/*.html` URLs are likewise JS-rendered shells (no document body) — those return 404 or a JS-only bootstrap screen.

So I went to the **authoritative implementation**: the Material Components for Android library (`material-components/material-components-android`, `master`), which is Google's reference implementation of Material 3 motion tokens. The numeric values below come from two upstream files that are machine-generated from Google's M3 design tokens (`Version: 34.0.0`):

- `lib/java/com/google/android/material/motion/res/values/tokens.xml` — the actual ms / control-point values
- `lib/java/com/google/android/material/motion/res/values/attrs.xml` — the descriptions of each tier
- `lib/java/com/google/android/material/transition/Material*.java` — which token each pattern binds to
- `lib/java/com/google/android/material/theme/res/values/themes_base.xml` — confirms `Theme.Material3` maps `motionDurationLong1` → `@integer/m3_sys_motion_duration_long1`, etc.

These are the literal numbers shipped in `com.google.android.material`. They are the canonical M3 values; the m3.material.io prose pages describe the same tokens.

---

## 1. The M3 duration + easing token tables (the canonical numbers)

### Durations (`motionDuration*`, integer ms) — from `tokens.xml`

| Token | ms | Tier purpose (per `attrs.xml`) |
|---|---|---|
| `motionDurationShort1` | **50** | small components (e.g. selection controls) |
| `motionDurationShort2` | **100** | small |
| `motionDurationShort3` | **150** | small |
| `motionDurationShort4` | **200** | small |
| `motionDurationMedium1` | **250** | medium transition area (e.g. expanding FAB) |
| `motionDurationMedium2` | **300** | medium |
| `motionDurationMedium3` | **350** | medium |
| `motionDurationMedium4` | **400** | medium |
| `motionDurationLong1` | **450** | large portion of screen |
| `motionDurationLong2` | **500** | large |
| `motionDurationLong3` | **550** | large |
| `motionDurationLong4` | **600** | large |
| `motionDurationExtraLong1` | **700** | ambient (auto-advancing carousel) |
| `motionDurationExtraLong2` | **800** | ambient |
| `motionDurationExtraLong3` | **900** | ambient |
| `motionDurationExtraLong4` | **1000** | ambient |

This is the M3 replacement for the old M2 "small / medium / large" duration buckets. **Tier = the {Short, Medium, Long, ExtraLong} family; severity = the index 1–4 inside it.** A "large" transition therefore picks one of `Long1..Long4` (450/500/550/600).

### Easings (`motionEasing*`) — exact control points from `tokens.xml`

| Easing attribute | cubic-bezier / path | When to use (per `attrs.xml`) |
|---|---|---|
| `motionEasingLinear` | `cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)` | simple fades |
| `motionEasingStandard` | `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)` | persistent elements (full in-out) |
| `motionEasingStandardDecelerate` | `cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0, 1)` | incoming element enters |
| `motionEasingStandardAccelerate` | `cubic-bezier(0.3, 0, 1, 1)` | outgoing element leaves |
| `motionEasingEmphasized` | **path**, NOT a single cubic-bezier: `M 0,0 C 0.05,0,0.133333,0.06,0.166666,0.4 C 0.208333,0.82,0.25,1,1,1` | persistent elements, emphasized (full in-out) |
| `motionEasingEmphasizedDecelerate` | `cubic-bezier(0.1, 0.7, 0.1, 1)` | incoming element enters |
| `motionEasingEmphasizedAccelerate` | `cubic-bezier(0.3, 0, 0.8, 0.2)` | outgoing element leaves |
| `motionEasingLegacy` (fastOutSlowIn) | `cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)` | pre-M3 fallback |

**Key gotcha:** M3's "Emphasized" easing is a **two-segment SVG path**, not a single cubic-bezier. A CSS `transition-timing-function: cubic-bezier(...)` cannot express it exactly. To use it on the web you either (a) use a JS animation lib that accepts a path / multi-keyframe easing (e.g. Motion One `"path(M 0,0 C …)"`, or Web Animations API with 3 keyframes), or (b) accept the closest single-cubic approximation `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)` (= M3 *Standard*), or the legacy `cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)` (fastOutSlowIn). In the MDC-Android code, when the theme's emphasis interpolator can't be resolved, `MaterialContainerTransform` falls back to `AnimationUtils.FAST_OUT_SLOW_IN_INTERPOLATOR` = `cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)`.

---

## 2. The four pattern bindings (the actual answer you asked for)

These come from each `Material*.java` transition class's `getDurationThemeAttrResId(appearing)` and `getEasingThemeAttrResId(appearing)` overrides — i.e. which token each pattern binds to.

### Pattern 1 — Container transform / shared element (`MaterialContainerTransform`)

Source: `MaterialContainerTransform.maybeApplyThemeValues`:

```java
maybeApplyThemeInterpolator(this, ctx, R.attr.motionEasingEmphasizedInterpolator,
    AnimationUtils.FAST_OUT_SLOW_IN_INTERPOLATOR);
maybeApplyThemeDuration(this, ctx, entering ? R.attr.motionDurationLong2
                                            : R.attr.motionDurationMedium4);
```

| Phase | Duration | Easing |
|---|---|---|
| Enter (expanding) | **500 ms** (`motionDurationLong2`) | Emphasized (path), fallback `cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1)` |
| Return (collapsing) | **400 ms** (`motionDurationMedium4`) | Emphasized (path), same fallback |

Plus the container's default fade-progress thresholds: **enter** fade happens over `0.00 → 0.25` of progress; **return** fade over `0.60 → 0.90` of progress. Default scrim color `0x52000000` (black 32%). Default `FadeMode = FADE_MODE_IN`.

### Pattern 2 — Fade through (`MaterialFadeThrough`)  ← the one you actually need

Source: `MaterialFadeThrough.java`:

```java
DEFAULT_THEMED_DURATION_ATTR = R.attr.motionDurationLong1;          // 450ms
DEFAULT_THEMED_EASING_ATTR   = R.attr.motionEasingEmphasizedInterpolator;
DEFAULT_START_SCALE = 0.92f;       // incoming scales 0.92 → 1.0
```

And `FadeThroughProvider.java`:

```java
static final float FADE_THROUGH_THRESHOLD = 0.35F;   // split point within the 450ms envelope
```

| Phase | Duration | Easing | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|
| Outgoing (disappear) | **450 ms total envelope**; outgoing fade occupies `0.0 → 0.35` of it → **≈ 157.5 ms** of actual fade | Emphasized (path) | pure alpha fade → 0; **no scale** on outgoing (`scaleOnDisappear = false`) |
| Incoming (appear) | same 450 ms envelope; incoming alpha + scale occupy `0.35 → 1.0` → **≈ 292.5 ms** | Emphasized (path) | alpha 0→1 **and** scale `0.92 → 1.0` |

So **for your task→task swap of (instruction card + sketch preview): use a single 450 ms `MaterialFadeThrough` envelope with the Emphasized path easing; the outgoing panel fades out (no scale) in the first 35% (~158 ms), then the incoming panel fades in *and* scales up from 0.92→1.0 over the remaining 65% (~293 ms).** Both halves share the one 450 ms emphasized curve — they're sequential sub-ranges of it, not two independent transitions.

CSS/web approximation if you can't use the SVG path:
```css
transition: opacity 450ms cubic-bezier(.2,0,0,1), transform 450ms cubic-bezier(.2,0,0,1);
/* outgoing: opacity 1→0 over ~158ms, then incoming: opacity 0→1 + scale .92→1 over ~293ms */
```

### Pattern 3 — Fade (`MaterialFade`)

Source: `MaterialFade.java`:

```java
DEFAULT_THEMED_INCOMING_DURATION_ATTR = R.attr.motionDurationMedium4;        // 400
DEFAULT_THEMED_OUTGOING_DURATION_ATTR = R.attr.motionDurationShort3;         // 150
DEFAULT_THEMED_INCOMING_EASING_ATTR   = R.attr.motionEasingEmphasizedDecelerateInterpolator; // cubic-bezier(.1,.7,.1,1)
DEFAULT_THEMED_OUTGOING_EASING_ATTR   = R.attr.motionEasingEmphasizedAccelerateInterpolator; // cubic-bezier(.3,0,.8,.2)
DEFAULT_START_SCALE = 0.8f;
DEFAULT_FADE_END_THRESHOLD_ENTER = 0.3f;     // incoming fade completes at 30% of progress
```

| Phase | Duration | Easing (exact cubic-bezier) | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|
| Incoming | **400 ms** (`motionDurationMedium4`) | **`cubic-bezier(0.1, 0.7, 0.1, 1)`** (Emphasized decelerate) | alpha 0→1, fade completes by 30% of progress, **scale 0.8 → 1.0**; no scale on disappear |
| Outgoing | **150 ms** (`motionDurationShort3`) | **`cubic-bezier(0.3, 0, 0.8, 0.2)`** (Emphasized accelerate) | pure alpha fade |

Note the asymmetry: incoming is **much slower** (400 ms, decelerate) than outgoing (150 ms, accelerate). That is intentional — Material enters gently, exits snappy.

### Pattern 4 — Scale (`MaterialElevationScale`)

Source: `MaterialElevationScale.java`:

```java
private static final float DEFAULT_SCALE = 0.85f;
// scaleProvider setOutgoingEndScale(0.85) + setIncomingStartScale(0.85)
// secondary provider = FadeProvider
```

`MaterialElevationScale` **does not override** `getDurationThemeAttrResId` / `getEasingThemeAttrResId` — they inherit `MaterialVisibility`'s defaults, which return `NO_ATTR_RES_ID` for both, with `getDefaultEasingInterpolator` = `AnimationUtils.FAST_OUT_SLOW_IN_INTERPOLATOR`. So Scale has **no theme-driven duration/easing of its own**; it is meant to be paired with a `MaterialContainerTransform` (as the exit/reenter transition of the outgoing/incoming screens) and inherits the duration you set on it. The numbers that ship in the M3 reference usage:

| Phase | Default duration (when paired with a container transform) | Default easing |
|---|---|---|
| Incoming (growing, `0.85 → 1.0`) | set by caller; canonical = **400 ms** (`motionDurationMedium4`), to mirror a container-transform return | `cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)` (fastOutSlowIn) — legacy default; substitute Emphasized path for M3 |
| Outgoing (shrinking, `1.0 → 0.85`) | same as above | same |

The "Scale" pattern in MDC is paired with container transform; it's not a stand-alone screen transition the way Fade/FadeThrough are.

### Shared axis (`MaterialSharedAxis`) — for reference, since you asked for the choosing guidance below

Source: `MaterialSharedAxis.java`:

```java
DEFAULT_THEMED_DURATION_ATTR = R.attr.motionDurationLong1;          // 450ms
DEFAULT_THEMED_EASING_ATTR   = R.attr.motionEasingEmphasizedInterpolator;
```

| Phase | Duration | Easing |
|---|---|---|
| Both axes (X / Y / Z), incoming & outgoing | **450 ms** (`motionDurationLong1`) | Emphasized (path) |

X = horizontal slide+fade, Y = vertical slide+fade, Z = scale+fade.

---

## 3. Choosing guidance (Fade through vs Shared axis vs Container transform)

This is the explicit purpose text from `attrs.xml` + the class Javadoc of each `Material*` transition:

- **Container transform (`MaterialContainerTransform`)** — use **when one element expands into another and they share a semantic identity** (a list item → its detail page; a FAB → a sheet; a card → full-screen). The container morphs size/shape/position; contents cross-fade (or fade-through) inside it. The Javadoc: *"A shared element Transition that transforms one container to another… can be used to morph between two Activities, Fragments, Views or a View to a Fragment."* Don't use it for swapping independent unrelated content.

- **Shared axis (`MaterialSharedAxis`)** — use **for siblings that share a spatial axis**, i.e. peer-level navigation along one direction: paging forward/back through a wizard, tabs in a top app bar, a master→detail push along X, a drill-down along Z. The shared axis implies the two states are *peers in the same space*. Pick the axis that matches the hierarchy direction (X = lateral, Y = vertical, Z = forward/back depth).

- **Fade through (`MaterialFadeThrough`)** — use **to switch between siblings that do NOT share a spatial relationship or where one surface fully replaces another** (per the class Javadoc: "fades out and in views sequentially" with a deliberate **35% gap** so they never cross-fade). This is exactly a task→task transition where the *whole instruction card + sketch preview area* is replaced by a new task's panel — peer siblings, no shared container, no consistent slide direction. Fade-through's 35% temporal gap is the deliberate signal "old is gone before new arrives" (unlike a cross-fade, which would imply a relationship).

- **Fade (`MaterialFade`)** — use for **transient entrances/exits within the same hierarchy**, e.g. a dialog, menu, or tooltip appearing/disappearing — not for swapping primary surfaces. Asymmetric (400 ms in decelerate vs 150 ms out accelerate).

- **Scale (`MaterialElevationScale`)** — use to emphasize an **elevation change** for the outgoing/incoming screen paired with a container transform (scale `0.85`), not as a standalone swapping transition.

**Rule of thumb for your case (task instruction + sketch preview swap):**
- Same region fully replaces itself with new content, peer siblings, no shared container morph, no consistent axis → **Fade through** is the right pattern. 450 ms / Emphasized path.

---

## 4. Combining the transition with a toast / snackbar immediately after

There is no combined-transition gl" guidance text in the transition classes themselves, but the canonical snackbar motion facts (from `BaseTransientBottomBar.java`) are:

```java
// Slide mode (default):
animationSlideDuration   = motionDurationLong2  → 500 ms (default fallback 250)
animationSlideInterpolator = FAST_OUT_SLOW_IN   → cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)
DEFAULT_ANIMATION_FADE_DURATION = 180  // content-fade within the slide (LINEAR)

// Fade mode:
animationFadeInDuration  = motionDurationLong2   → 500 ms (default 150)   easing LINEAR, scale 0.8→1 with LINEAR_OUT_SLOW_IN (cubic-bezier(0,0,0.2,1))
animationFadeOutDuration  = motionDurationMedium1 → 250 ms (default 75)    easing LINEAR
```

So a Material 3 snackbar itself takes **500 ms to enter** (slide, fastOutSlowIn) and **250 ms to exit**.

**Practical combining guidance (derived from the motion principles, not a literal spec sentence):**

1. **Don't start competing motions in the same direction simultaneously.** Your fade-through occupies the panel region for 450 ms. If a snackbar slides up from the bottom at the same time, you get two unrelated fade/slide motions reading as noise.
2. **Trigger the snackbar after the fade-through completes.** Deliver the new task panel first (450 ms), then bring the snackbar in. A clean schedule:
   - t = 0 → 450 ms: `MaterialFadeThrough` swapping the panel (Emphasized path)
   - t ≈ 450–480 ms (one frame + ~30 ms gap): fire the snackbar
   - t ≈ 480–980 ms: snackbar slide-in, 500 ms, `cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)`
   - snackbar dwell (LENGTH_SHORT ≈ 1500 ms / LENGTH_LONG ≈ 2750 ms)
   - snackbar exit: 250 ms, LINEAR fade
   - **total perceived cadence ≈ 950 ms entrance sequence** before the user is "settled" on the new task with its confirmation toast visible.
3. **Use Emphasized-accelerate on the outgoing element, Emphasized-decelerate (or the Emphasized full path) on the incoming**, matching what the pattern classes already do (MaterialFade: out=cubic-bezier(0.3,0,0.8,0.2), in=cubic-bezier(0.1,0.7,0.1,1)). The snackbar's slide uses fastOutSlowIn (≈ Standard), which reads as a *different* family from the fade-through's Emphasized — that visual distinction is good: it keeps the toast perceptually separate from the task swap.

---

## 5. Quick-reference for your single requested case

> **Fade-through swap of "task instruction card + sketch preview area"**

- **Duration:** 450 ms total envelope (`motionDurationLong1`)
- **Easing:** Emphasized path `M 0,0 C 0.05,0,0.133333,0.06,0.166666,0.4 C 0.208333,0.82,0.25,1,1,1`
  - CSS fallback: `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)` (M3 Standard — closest single cubic) or `cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)` (legacy fastOutSlowIn, which is what MDC-Android falls back to)
- **Internal split:** outgoing fade occupies first 35% (~158 ms, no scale); incoming fade + scale `0.92 → 1.0` occupies last 65% (~293 ms)
- **If a snackbar/toast confirms the new task:** fire it at ~480 ms (after the fade-through completes), with a 500 ms slide using `cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)`.
